subject: Clarify SBOM provenance, pen-test summary, and patch SLA (Borealis Bank RFP)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@borealisbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@borealisbank.com
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RFP - SBOM provenance, pen test exec summary, and patch SLA

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the initial RFP packet. As part of Borealis Bank's procurement checklist we need a bit more granularity on three items before we proceed to legal redlines:

1) SBOM provenance: can you confirm the build pipeline(s) used to generate SBOM artifacts (tooling, source-of-truth for dependency versions, frequency of regeneration, and whether SBOMs are signed)? We need to map third-party component risk to our supply chain process.

2) Penetration testing: please provide an executive summary of the most recent pen test (scope, critical/ high findings, remediation status and timelines). If you have a one-page summary that includes CVE references that would be ideal.

3) Patch SLAs: Borealis requires a suggested SLA table for patching vulnerabilities classified as critical/ high/ medium with expected timelines for deployable mitigations and for full remediation, along with the process for emergency patching. Is Redwood able to commit to 30/90 day SLAs for Critical/High?

We'd like to close these clarifications by EOD Tuesday to keep the RFP cadence.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Sr. InfoSec Manager | Borealis Bank

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@borealisbank.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP - SBOM provenance, pen test exec summary, and patch SLA

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask. I'm attaching a concise package we prepared for RFPs that hits each point (SBOM manifest, pen-test executive summary, and a draft patch SLA proposal). High level responses inline below; full attachments are included.

SBOM provenance:
- We generate SBOMs from the canonical build pipeline for our public and private deployments. We use Syft for inventory + a reproducible build step that records git commit SHAs used for each component and container image. SBOMs are regenerated on every release and on any dependency update; we also publish quarterly SBOM snapshots for procurement teams.
- SBOM artifacts are signed using our internal key management service (KMS) and the signing metadata is included in the manifest (signature algorithm: RSA-PSS). The attached CSV includes a sample artifact with provenance columns (repo, commit, build-id, timestamp, signature).

Pen test executive summary:
- Last full-scope external pen test: 2026-06 (third-party vendor: RedHarbor Security). Scope: control plane APIs, tenant isolation layers, authentication flows, and hosted management console.
- Findings: 0 critical, 2 high (one web session token misconfiguration, one privilege escalation vector in a secondary admin tool — both mitigated), 6 medium, 11 low. Remediation status: high findings fully remediated in the June patch release (2026-06-21); mediums are scheduled across the July and August sprints; details and CVE mapping are in the attached PDF.

Patch SLA proposal (draft):
- Critical: initial mitigation within 48 hours, full remediation and customer patch within 30 days (exceptions logged and escalated to Exec Sponsor).
- High: initial mitigation within 7 days, full remediation within 60 days.
- Medium: initial mitigation/mitigating controls within 30 days, full remediation within 120 days.

We generally commit to the 30/90 model for Critical/High only when the vulnerability affects our hosted control plane or dedicated pool images under a purchase agreement with Reserved Capacity and explicit exception handling; for private/on-prem installs, timelines depend on customer change windows and a mutually agreed maintenance window.

I'll loop in our security lead (cc'ing Neha) to confirm any additional evidentiary materials you might need. If you'd like us to move Critical -> 30 days for full remediation by contract, we can make a limited SLA commitment under the Enterprise Addendum with defined exceptions (zero-day coordination, third-party upstream fixes, and customer-side exposure).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
attachments: sbom-manifest-20260917.csv, pen-test-exec-summary-202608.pdf, patch-sla-proposal-20260921.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP - SBOM provenance, pen test exec summary, and patch SLA

Jordan / Priyom —

Quick internal note on the SLA language before we send a formal redline:
- For Critical: redwood can guarantee deployable mitigations within 48 hours for hosted API and Dedicated customers (we have automated rollback and patch pipelines tied to canary gating). Committing to full remediation in 30 days is reasonable but we need to add carve-outs for upstream library fixes where mitigation requires a third-party patch.
- For High: 60 days for full remediation is aggressive but acceptable for hosted. For Dedicated/reserved pools we should be explicit that mitigation cadence may be subject to scheduled maintenance windows; recommend we add an "SLA exception" bucket that requires advance notice and joint remediation plan.
- SBOM signing: ensure the SBOM manifest includes both the build-id and the KMS signature thumbprint; customers sometimes ask for a verification script — we can provide one as a support artifact.

I also recommend attaching the pen test remediation tracker (internal) but strip internal-only notes. The external exec summary we provide must not include developer JIRA IDs or internal patch comments.

Neha
Head of Security Assurance | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP - SBOM provenance, pen test exec summary, and patch SLA

Noted — I'll prepare a redlined SLA document that includes:
- Explicit "Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private" rows for timelines
- Exception definitions (upstream patches, customer-controlled images, regulatory freeze windows)
- Escalation path (SE -> Security -> CTO -> Exec Sponsor) and crediting language for missed SLAs

I'll sanitize the remediation tracker and produce a 1-page CVE mapping table to include with the pen-test exec summary. Will send the redline by Monday.

-Priyom
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@borealisbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP - SBOM provenance, pen test exec summary, and patch SLA

Elena —

Following up with the updated materials (attached) and a short summary of changes based on your questions:

- SBOM manifest: included signed sample CSV + verification steps. Regeneration cadence: per-release + quarterly snapshots; signature uses KMS with RSA-PSS thumbprint included.
- Pen test exec summary: sanitized redacted PDF (no internal JIRA IDs), includes CVE mapping and confirmation that the two High findings were remediated in the June release; a 1-page CVE table is attached as part of the PDF.
- Patch SLA: attached is our proposed SLA workbook that separates Hosted / Dedicated / Private timelines and defines exceptions and the escalation path. Key offer: for Hosted + Redwood Dedicated under an enterprise commitment we can contractually commit to a 30-day full remediation for Critical issues and 90 days for High (subject to the exceptions outlined). For Private deployments we propose joint change-window SLAs.

Next steps: if this package satisfies your procurement team we'll accept a single redline from Borealis Legal on the Enterprise Addendum and SLA exhibit; otherwise happy to set a 30-minute call to walk through any remaining items.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
attachments: sbom-manifest-20260917.csv, pen-test-exec-summary-202608.pdf, patch-sla-proposal-20260921.xlsx
